# ADR-063 — Checkpoint 9.4: dependable recurring tasks and reminders — one successor rule, snooze as an occurrence property, per-occurrence reminders (migration 0018)

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Checkpoint 9.4 — recurring tasks and reminders are dependable end to end: one successor rule for every writer, snooze as an occurrence property, per-occurrence reminders with foregrounding actions (2026-09-14, owner-directed).** One migration, `0018` (`occurrences.snoozed_until timestamptz`, level **19**), justified under the migration policy as durable state that no zero-migration alternative could guarantee: moving `occurs_at` breaks the row's identity (the nightly job re-inserts the original instant as a duplicate), pushing the date into `recurrence_exdates` mutates the rule, and PATCHing the parent's `due_at` re-anchors the whole series. **1. THE SUCCESSOR CONTRACT.** A completion-anchored successor is `local date of the completion + INTERVAL` at the completed row's own wall-clock time in `recurrence_timezone`, by pure calendar arithmetic (DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY/YEARLY; month-end clamped to the target month, so done Jan 31 → Feb 28 and done Feb 28 → Mar 28 — the drift to the 28th is accepted and documented; "I meant month-end" is what `due_date` + `BYMONTHDAY=-1` is for), and **strictly after the completed row's own instant** (`after`, an exclusive lower bound). The strictly-after rule exists because a completion INTERVAL days early would otherwise compute the completed row's own `occurs_at`, and `occurrences_parent_occurs_at_key` would then silently swallow the insert in every writer — found by two independent adversarial reviewers as a 9.4 regression before it shipped. All five writers — API complete/skip, the worker re-check, the nightly repair, PATCH re-seed and task reopen — call one function with one shared `wallTimeOfNaiveTimestamp` reader, so they compute the identical instant and the belt-and-braces insert is a true no-op. **A collision that leaves no open occurrence is never reported as success**: the API warns ids-only and still enqueues the re-check, the worker re-reads state and throws (→ retries → dead letter → alert), and the nightly repair counts the parent as failed with `reason: collision` (→ `OccurrencesJobError` → the existing `expand-window.dead:<UTC date>` key, ADR-058/062). **2. NIGHTLY REPAIR.** `occurrences.expand-window` gains phase 2: every open, unarchived completion-anchored parent with no scheduled occurrence and terminal history gets its successor inserted idempotently from its latest terminal row, per-parent contained. This is the durable recovery ADR-062 left open for "completion commits but the successor is lost"; `bossReady=false` at the API is no longer a loss at all (the successor is in-transaction since 9.3), and `boss.send` failing after the commit is a warn + 200 rather than a 500 for a recorded completion. **3. THE SERIES ANCHOR.** `resolveSeriesAnchor` = `due_at ?? min(occurs_at) ?? now`, floored to whole seconds (a millisecond anchor made the first expanded instance sort before `now` and vanish), used by POST /tasks, capture commit, PATCH branch A and the nightly job alike, and POST/capture now persist it as `due_at` so no writer can disagree; an unchanged effective rule (normalised, part-order-insensitive) causes no occurrence churn on PATCH. Today never buckets a recurring parent by that anchor (`isNull(tasks.rrule)`, the Agenda precedent) — before 9.4 a monthly task whose next instance was more than seven days out surfaced as a stale Overdue parent. `due_date` rules are validated at POST/PATCH (400, token only: `unsupported_frequency` / `embedded_until_count` / `invalid_rrule`); sub-daily frequencies and embedded UNTIL/COUNT are refused. **4. SNOOZE.** `POST /occurrences/:id/snooze {until}` sets only `snoozed_until` (bounded to 31 days; task-only, `409 occurrence_not_task`; terminal rows `409 occurrence_not_open`). The effective instant is `greatest(occurs_at, snoozed_until)` in one shared SQL helper feeding Today, Agenda, review contexts, project summaries and `/tasks/:id/complete`'s redirect — a snooze may only DEFER; a day-before reminder snoozed by an hour moves the reminder, never the due. A rule edit regenerates future rows and their snoozes with them (documented). Snooze chips and notification actions compute their targets in the DEVICE zone (ADR rule 4: the task's zone is display-only). **5. REOPEN.** `POST /occurrences/:id/reopen` flips the parent's LATEST terminal row back to scheduled (older rows `409 occurrence_not_reopenable`; dropped/archived parents `409 task_not_open`; task-only). For a completion-anchored parent it withdraws every other scheduled row in the same transaction — the open successor is derived state, and the partial unique index forbids two open lazy rows — reporting `withdrawn_successor_id`; it never creates a successor. `POST /tasks/:id/reopen` on a recurring parent now guarantees an open occurrence (seed or window) in the same transaction. **6. REMINDERS.** `GET /reminders` derives one reminder per open occurrence from the parent's `remind_at` wall clock and its signed day-offset from `due_at`, resolved in `recurrence_timezone` (DST-safe by construction), `snoozed_until` overriding; one-off tasks keep a one-hour grace, derived reminders are strictly future (a freshly generated successor must not fire instantly). The primary device schedules from that feed with deterministic identifiers `reminder:<key>:<instant>`, a `reminder` category with **Done / Snooze 1h / Tomorrow 9am**, all `opensAppToForeground: true` — verified in the installed expo-notifications 57.0.12 source that a non-foregrounding action is parked in a static in-process list and lost when the process is dead (the ADR-060 direct-reply finding applies to plain buttons), while a foregrounding action is delivered exactly like the default tap already proven cold-start on the Rabbit R1. Responses are deduped on `${identifier}:${actionIdentifier}` (expo's own hook collapses same-identifier responses), released on failure so a retry works; every task/occurrence mutation cancels the scheduled entry and dismisses the presented one for its key; pre-9.4 alarms are replaced once with the category. **7. UI.** Presets only — Never / Daily / Weekdays / Weekly (explicit BYDAY) / Monthly (BYMONTHDAY, `-1` for a month-end due date) / Every N days — plus "after I complete it" (completion anchor, FREQ+INTERVAL only); the Phase 4 editor stays reachable behind "Edit advanced…" for custom rules and is never clobbered. **Unchanged and reaffirmed:** ADR-013, ADR-019/020 (local reminders on the explicit primary device), ADR-031, ADR-058's dedupe-key contract, ADR-060 (no `expo-task-manager`), ADR-062. **Recorded, not fixed:** nonexistent spring-forward wall-clock times resolve one hour early (pre-existing `date-fns-tz` behaviour, now inherited by derived reminders); a 90-day window that crosses a fall-back yields 90 rather than 91 rows; `MAX_SNOOZE_DAYS` is elapsed days; reminder titles are unbounded (user-authored, local only). **Phase 9's next checkpoint is not decided by this ADR** (Checkpoint 9.4, 2026-09-14)
